review: The hymn is the rapture and the resurrection: 1:1–4 is 1 Thess 4:16 with Matt 24:31, 2:1–4 is 1 Thess 4:17 (בַּעֲנָנִים … בַּחֲטִיפָה) with 2 Thess 1:7, 3:1–4 is 1 Cor 15:55 (אַיֵּה עָקְצְךָ) nearly verbatim with Hos 13:14, and 4:1–4 is Rev 19:1–6 with Rev 21:4.
3:1 keeps the direct address to death, as Paul's taunt does, with the second-person suffix on עֹקֶץ; the Hebrew uses the feminine form of the Arabic مُوت ('O death'), matching the gender of מָוֶת.
2:4 uses מְרִיעִים (the shout of Ps 47:2) for the Arabic هَاتِفِين, so the triumph over the foes is the psalm's jubilation and not a war-cry.
